Bangladesh is an agricultural country where about 50 percent of its people are farmers. Through their hard work, the country is filled with a rich abundance of crops, which feeds our population. By exporting these crops, our economy grows stronger. Simply put, the farmer is the key to our national progress and the very life of our nation.

Agriculture and its farmers are deeply tied to the soil of Bangladesh. These hard-working people provide food for the entire nation day after day. Since our economic structure depends on agriculture, the nation's economy is built upon the sacrifices and intense labor of our farmers. They continue to serve the country and its people while enduring poverty, hardship, and social neglect. In every village of Bangladesh, you will find these farmers. Before the sun even rises, they head to the fields with plows on their shoulders. Working through the hot sun and heavy rain, they grow crops with endless dedication from morning until evening. By working tirelessly, they produce food grains and other essential crops for everyone.

Farmers make constant efforts to meet the food demands of our country. Because of their hard work, fields are always full of crops. Many large factories also depend on them, as the items grown by farmers serve as raw materials for various industries. Furthermore, when there is an extra harvest beyond what the country needs, it is exported abroad to earn valuable foreign currency. Farmers provide food for people at all levels of society, whether rich or poor.

In ancient times, the population of this country was small, and there was plenty of land. The fertile soil produced large amounts of crops. At that time, nearly 95 percent of the population were farmers. Their granaries were full of grain, their sheds were full of cattle, and their ponds were full of fish. Their lives were peaceful and prosperous. However, everything changed when British rule began in Bengal, bringing heavy taxes and unfair laws that oppressed the farming community.

Although Bangladesh has been independent for over five decades, no major positive change has occurred in the lives of our poor farmers. Many farmers in Bengal still live without proper education, clothes, or healthcare. Their lives remain filled with sorrow and financial struggle. As they grow old, a lack of medical care reduces their ability to work. Consequently, the burden of supporting the family falls on their children. This often forces the children to quit school, trapping the next generation in the same cycle of poverty and ignorance.

The population of our country is growing rapidly, which means agricultural land is shrinking. At the same time, the fertility of the soil has decreased. As a result, it is becoming much harder for farmers to grow enough food for everyone. Furthermore, while farming methods have improved across the world, many places in our country still use old, traditional tools. Farmers also lack the resources and modern strategies needed to deal with natural disasters like droughts, heavy rains, and floods. On top of that, due to a lack of education, dishonest people often cheat them, which makes their financial situation even worse.

To improve the lives of our farmers, we must introduce scientific methods to our agriculture. The government should provide interest-free loans, access to education, and free healthcare services for farming families. Only when we support them in these areas can their living standards truly improve.

To meet the rising demand for food, we must bring modern technology into farming. Using updated methods will help increase crop production. We can modernize this sector by providing farmers with high-quality seeds, better irrigation systems, modern machinery, and proper fertilizers.

Agriculture is the foundation of our economy. The crops grown by farmers increase our national income and support economic growth. They ensure food security for the entire country and provide nutritious foods like fruits, vegetables, and pulses that keep the population healthy. Additionally, industries that rely on crops like jute, sugarcane, and cotton can only thrive because of the raw materials our farmers supply.

The farmer is one of the most important members of our society because their hard work feeds the nation. Yet, despite their massive contribution, many farmers are still denied proper respect and financial stability. Even though our survival depends entirely on their work, they are still looked down upon by society.

In recent years, steps have been taken to modernize agriculture, making the lives of farmers a bit easier. The government has distributed thousands of agricultural machines across various districts at discounted prices. Furthermore, specialized tools invented by local research institutes are being provided to farmers with significant financial subsidies.

Agriculture is the backbone of our economy. If we want to keep this backbone strong and help our country progress, we must prioritize the development of agriculture and the welfare of our farmers. Otherwise, national growth will stall. The government cannot handle this huge responsibility alone. It is a duty that belongs to every citizen. Therefore, alongside the government, we must all step forward to support and uplift our farmers.

<SUMM> Bangladesh is an agricultural country where about 50% of the population are farmers, making agriculture the backbone of the economy and farmers the key to national progress. Through their hard work, they produce food for the entire nation, supply raw materials to industries, export surplus crops to earn foreign currency, and contribute to food security, national income, and economic growth. Farmers work tirelessly from sunrise to sunset in every village despite poverty, hardship, and social neglect. In ancient times, when land was abundant and 95% of the people were farmers, they lived prosperous lives, but British rule imposed heavy taxes and unfair laws that worsened their condition. Even after independence, many farmers still lack proper education, healthcare, clothing, and financial security, forcing many children to leave school and continue the cycle of poverty. Rapid population growth, shrinking farmland, declining soil fertility, outdated farming methods, natural disasters, lack of modern equipment, and exploitation due to illiteracy further increase their difficulties. To improve their lives, scientific farming methods, modern technology, quality seeds, irrigation, machinery, fertilizers, interest-free loans, education, and free healthcare should be provided. In recent years, the government has taken steps by distributing subsidized agricultural machinery and locally developed farming tools, making agriculture more modern. Although farmers are among the most important members of society, they are still denied proper respect and financial stability despite feeding the nation. Therefore, both the government and every citizen must work together to develop agriculture, improve farmers' welfare, and strengthen the backbone of Bangladesh's economy for continued national progress. </SUMM>
